why_it_fails: It is bookkeeping: marking an approval done in zm changes nothing for anyone ('Cons: none'), and with its check wrong the asking agent records it done with its evidence itself (SPEC: zm ask check --evidence), so it is not a decision a person must make.

card.title: Mark the 'make the three machine images public' approval as done?
card.context: Yesterday you approved making Larder's three ready-made machine images public. They are public now: anyone can download them without logging in, and we tested all three. But zm still lists that approval as not done, because its automatic test looks for a version name that our build never uses. Marking it done only updates zm's list: nothing about the images changes.
card.question: Mark the 'make the three machine images public' approval as done?

choices.label: Mark it done
choices.pros: Clears it from your Decisions, with the download test results written on the record

choices.label: Leave it open
choices.cons: It stays in your Decisions as not done, since its test can never pass

card.why: The images really are public; the test only checks the wrong version name.

action.command: zm ask check demo --evidence 'all three download'
action.shown: If you choose A, zm runs zm ask check demo --evidence 'all three download' on bea-mac, as you.
